summary: Ketu's seven-year period is described by most texts as unsettled: quarrels, trouble from enemies, thieves or authorities, wounds, fevers, scandal, losses and living away from home. BPHS makes it good, even giving high position, land and family happiness, when Ketu is in a kendra, trikona or the 11th, in a benefic or own/exaltation sign, or in an upachaya house; bad in the 2nd, 8th or 12th or under malefic influence. Because Ketu owns no sign here, much depends on the sign it sits in, its sign lord and the planets joined with it.
themes: exile or living away from home
results borrowed from sign lord and associates
common_outcomes: trouble from enemies, thieves and the ruler, wounds from weapons, diseases from heat, false accusation and a stain on the family name, danger from fire, living away from home (Phaladeepika 19.17)
grief and confusion connected with women, trouble from powerful people, loss of wealth, improper conduct, exile, toothache, leg pain and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.25)
distress, failing judgement, various illnesses and growing physical trouble, a life of much misery with only slight comforts (Jataka Parijata 18.145)
when well placed: favour of rulers, headship of a village or region, vehicles, children, gains from abroad, happiness from the spouse and cattle (BPHS 47.72-74)
rare_outcomes: imprisonment, destruction of kinsmen and of the home, company of low people (BPHS 47.77, when badly placed)
attainment of a kingdom or high government position and opportunities to acquire elephants (BPHS 47.74-75, Ketu in the 3rd, 6th or 11th)
Raman (by sign): founding of sacred institutions (Gemini); misappropriation of funds and prosecution (Capricorn); travel by water to distant countries and respect there (Pisces)

by_area.personality: Failing judgement and distress (Jataka Parijata 18.145); anxiety and fear in the middle of the period (BPHS 47.75); in Raman's sign list, religious study, moral elevation and tolerance in Sagittarius or Pisces, pessimism and dependence in Aquarius.
by_area.career: Favour of rulers, headship of a place and high position when Ketu is in a kendra, trikona, the 11th or an upachaya (BPHS 47.72-75); trouble from the ruler, false accusation and scandal (Phaladeepika 19.17); trouble from powerful people (Phaladeepika 19.25); Raman: promotion and favour of superiors in Pisces, displeasure of superiors in Aquarius.
by_area.finance: Loss of wealth (Phaladeepika 19.25); gains of land, vehicles and cattle when well placed (BPHS 47.72-74); money comes in during the middle of the period (Jataka Parijata 18.157); abundant wealth if Ketu is aspected by a benefic (Jataka Parijata 18.155); waste of wealth through illness if joined with malefics (Jataka Parijata 18.156).
by_area.health: Wounds from weapons, heat diseases, danger from fire (Phaladeepika 19.17); toothache, leg pain, phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.25); various diseases and physical torment (Jataka Parijata 18.145); illness in the last part of the period (BPHS 47.76); disease when Ketu is in the 2nd, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.77).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from the spouse when well placed (BPHS 47.73-74); grief and confusion linked to women (Phaladeepika 19.25); Raman lists sickness or loss of the wife under several signs (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Capricorn).
by_area.family: Children and growth of the household when well placed (BPHS 47.73-74); elders and relatives fall ill at the start (Jataka Parijata 18.157); loss of kinsmen and of the home when badly placed (BPHS 47.77); stain on the family name (Phaladeepika 19.17).
by_area.spirituality: Raman's sign list stresses pilgrimage and religious study (Taurus), philosophical initiation (Cancer), philosophical debate (Leo), religious discussion (Sagittarius) and religious devotion (Pisces). Raman's list of Ketu's general significations includes religion, astrology and moksha (ch. XXIII). Rath calls Ketu the mokshakaraka.

strengtheners: Ketu in a kendra, trikona or the 11th, in a benefic sign, in its exaltation or own sign (BPHS 47.72)
aspected by a benefic, or in a benefic varga (BPHS 47.72, Sanskrit gloss)

Frawley (general Ketu, not dasha-specific): Ketu is weak when the lord of its sign is weak, when it is in the 3rd, 6th or 8th, or when aspected by malefics such as Saturn and Mars
lagna_or_context_notes: Ketu owns no sign in this library, so the texts route its results through other factors: Raman (ch. XXIII) says the nodes give the results of the lord of the sign they occupy; Rele (p. 64) and Jataka Parijata 18.155-156 say they act through the planets they join; Phaladeepika 20.52-53 makes them yogakarakas when tied to kendra or trikona lords. BPHS 47.3-4 says the nodes, being always retrograde, deliver the drekkana-based phase results in reverse order. P.V.R. Narasimha Rao (citing Sanjay Rath's 'tripod of life') judges a mahadasha mainly from the Sun's position, antardashas from the Moon and smaller periods from the lagna. No source read gives Ketu-mahadasha results counted from the Moon.

source_views.view: Ketu, the headless trunk. In a kendra, trikona or the 11th, in a benefic sign, or in its exaltation or own sign: good relations with the ruler, headship of a country or village, vehicles, children, gains from abroad, happiness from the wife, cattle. In the 3rd, 6th or 11th: a kingdom or high position, good friends, elephants. Raja yoga at the start, fear in the middle, illness and distant travel at the end. In the 2nd, 8th or 12th, or aspected by a malefic: imprisonment, loss of kinsmen and home, anxiety, company of low people, disease.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.35-36 and 47.71-77, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 35 makes Scorpio Ketu's exaltation and Sagittarius its moolatrikona; verse 36 gives Scorpio as its house, with Pisces according to some. Verse 72 lists kendra, 11th, trikona, benefic sign, benefic aspect, exaltation or benefic varga as alternatives. The gloss reads verse 76 as the 2nd, 8th or 12th together with malefic conjunction or aspect, and adds gains through low people in verse 77.
Results come at the start, middle or end of a period according to the planet's drekkana; for retrograde planets the order reverses, and the nodes are always retrograde.

19.17: trouble from enemies, thieves and the king, weapon wounds, heat diseases, false calumny, stigma to the family, fire, residence away from home. 19.25 (Vimshottari list): grief and confusion through women, trouble from the powerful, loss of wealth, improper acts, exile, toothache, leg pain, phlegm disorders.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.52-53 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri; printed numbering uneven)
source_views.view: Rahu and Ketu in a kendra or trikona and linked with the lord of either become yogakarakas; in a benefic's sign and linked with a planet they give good results.

Ketu's period brings distress, failing judgement, illness, physical torment and misdeeds, with slight comfort. Joined with a benefic it gives happiness; aspected by a benefic, abundant wealth; with malefics, danger through wicked people and illness that wastes wealth. Threefold course: elders and relatives ill at the start, money in the middle, happiness at the end.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 269-271
source_views.view: Results of Ketu's dasa by the sign it occupies, Aries to Pisces (recorded as conditional results). Sagittarius, Pisces and Leo come out best; Aries, Virgo, Capricorn and Aquarius worst.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XVI (p. 127) and ch. XXIII
source_views.view: Rahu and Ketu give good results in signs of benefics and evil in evil signs; as lustreless planets they give the results of the lords of the signs they occupy.

source_views.source: V.G. Rele, Directional Astrology of the Hindus, p. 64
source_views.view: The nodes own no houses. In kendras and trikonas they are always good; elsewhere their conjunctions give good or bad results according to the strength of the planet joined.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers ch. 6 (pp. 202-203) and Ketu treatment section (pp. 259-260)
source_views.view: The major lord sets the tone of the time; the start of a major or minor period is the time to balance a difficult lord by gem, mantra or deity, propitiating a malefic. For Ketu: cat's eye only when Ketu is strong; mantra OM KETAVE, seed OM KEM; worship of Rudra or the terrible forms of the Divine; the yoga of knowledge and self-inquiry.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach ch. 16 (16.5.3; Example 55)
source_views.view: Sun is the reference for a mahadasha, Moon for an antardasha, lagna for a pratyantardasha (Rath's tripod of life). In his example he treats Ketu as a lord of Scorpio (Ketu as lagna lord for a Scorpio ascendant), and cites Parashara that when one co-owner occupies a dual-owned sign the other acts as its main lord.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 78, 168, 221, 315
source_views.view: Ketu's deity is Ganapati (p. 168); Ketu is a co-lord of Scorpio (p. 315) and is called debilitated in Taurus (p. 221). Example charts only: death in Ketu dasa Venus sub-period as the seventh dasa of a long-lived native (p. 78); a war-time Ketu dasa read through Ganapati's protection (p. 221).

disagreements: Sign rulership and dignity: BPHS 47.35-36 gives Ketu exaltation in Scorpio, moolatrikona in Sagittarius and own sign Scorpio (Pisces by some); Rath and Narasimha Rao treat Ketu as co-lord of Scorpio and Rath calls it debilitated in Taurus; Rele (p. 64) and this library say the nodes own no houses, and the library's node dignity (exalted Taurus, debilitated Scorpio) is the reverse of BPHS for Ketu, so sign conditions are written by sign name here. BPHS 47.76-77: Santhanam reads the bad case as the 2nd, 8th or 12th OR malefic aspect; the Sanskrit gloss reads the houses together with malefic influence. Phases: BPHS puts raja yoga at the start, fear in the middle and illness and travel at the end; Jataka Parijata puts illness of elders at the start, money in the middle and happiness at the end. Tone: BPHS and Jataka Parijata 18.155 allow strongly good results, while Phaladeepika 19 and Jataka Parijata 18.145 give only troubles. Raman's 3rd/6th/11th rule (good) contrasts with Frawley's general view that the 3rd, 6th and 8th weaken Ketu.
phrasing_guidance: Describe the period as one of withdrawal, sudden changes and tests, with real gains possible when the chart shows the listed good placements. Lead with what the chart supports (sign, house, sign lord, companions) rather than the generic list of troubles. Avoid predicting imprisonment, the death of relatives or specific diseases; frame health items as reasons for care. Remedies can be offered as traditional practices, not as guarantees.

Jataka Parijata 18.157: elders and relatives fall ill at the start, money comes in the middle, happiness at the end.
